chunks: ʿAlī narrated from his father, from al-Nawfalī, from al-Sukūnī, from Abī ʿAbd Allāh عليه السلام, who said:

Amīr al-Muʾminīn عليه السلام said: “Do not intercede for anyone in a hadd punishment once it has reached the Imam, for he possesses authority over it. But intercede in what has not yet reached the Imam when you see blood, and intercede before the Imam in matters other than the hadd with the consent of the one for whom intercession is sought. And do not intercede concerning the right of any Muslim man or anyone else except with his permission.”

key_terms.الدَّمَ: bloodshed or a case involving blood
key_terms.الْإِمَامَ: the legitimate authority who adjudicates and enforces legal rulings
key_terms.الْمَشْفُوعِ لَهُ: the person on whose behalf intercession is made
key_terms.تَشْفَعَنَّ: to intercede or plead on behalf of someone
key_terms.حَدٍّ: a legally prescribed punishment in sacred law

ai.seo_question: When is intercession permitted or forbidden in hadd cases and personal rights according to Amīr al-Muʾminīn عليه السلام?
ai.summary: This hadith sets limits on shafa'ah in judicial matters. It forbids intercession in hadd cases once they have formally reached the Imam, while permitting intercession before that stage or in non-hadd matters with proper consent. It also emphasizes that the rights of individuals cannot be negotiated without their permission.
